amendments.change: status NOT APPLICABLE; the reading 'row count explains it' is withdrawn; the interpolated numbers are kept under interpolation_not_used
amendments.reason_user: The registered interpolation is linear in log row count between the bracketing saturation sizes, which presumes the curve is approximately linear in log row count between them. The measured curve (378, 376, 455, 382, 214) turns over at or near 10k (the rise from 3k to 10k and the fall from 10k to 30k are each about 5 SE), with the 10k and 30k seed ranges barely overlapping, so its 442.9 is a property of the straight line rather than an estimate of the curve at 11,955 rows. The direct matched-size measurement at exactly 11,955 rows (468 +/- 25) is the valid comparator and supersedes it.
amendments.reason_user_original: The registered interpolation is linear in log row count between the bracketing saturation sizes. That presumes monotonicity between them. The measured curve (378, 376, 455, 382, 214) has a real peak between 10k and 30k, with the 10k and 30k seed ranges barely overlapping, so the interpolation crosses a hump and its 442.9 is a property of the straight line rather than an estimate of the curve at 11,955 rows. The direct matched-size measurement at exactly 11,955 rows (468 +/- 25) is the valid comparator and supersedes it.

data: TR0 + TS0 canonical-pair bpRNA reference structures (mxfold2_datasets, CC BY 4.0); Rfam 15.1 seed rows exactly as in runs/2026-10-07_turner_nullspace_rfam_r2 for the control and saturation

predictions.C2: every reported null basis vector moves no row by more than 1e-9; the worst row change is reported

T1.fact_recorded_before_running: TR0 is NOT shorter than Rfam: median length 105 nt (max 498) vs Rfam's 84 (max 4,065), profiled read-only before registration
T1.operational: 0 < nontrivial < 214 in every configuration ('nontrivial' already excludes the 2 (d0) or 3 (d2) intrinsic directions)
T1.prior_claude: likely refuted on the 'below 214' side: a random 62% subsample of Rfam rows had MORE nontrivial directions (287.4 +- 5.4) than the full set, and TR0+TS0 is about 11% of Rfam's rows; uncertain, because fewer rows also use fewer columns
T1.rule_user: The TR0-restricted nontrivial dimension is below Rfam's 214, because TR0 has fewer families and shorter sequences, and above the intrinsic 2.

predictions.anchor_check: the whole distinct pair-bearing Rfam population in d0_special_hp0 must reproduce the full Rfam set's nontrivial dimension exactly (unpaired rows have zero count vectors; duplicates cannot change a rank)
predictions.context_point_rule: the existing 67,418-row Rfam subsamples (drawn from NOMINAL rows) are 'effectively on the curve' only if the expected number of distinct pair-bearing rows in such a draw is within 1% of 67,418; otherwise they stay context
predictions.inherited: exact reconstruction on every row (any failure stops the run), C0, C1, C3, C4, R5, R6, agreement of the dimension methods
predictions.joint_read: d0_special_hp0: interpolate the saturation run's seed-mean nontrivial dimension, and its seed SD, linearly in log row count between the two saturation sizes bracketing TR0+TS0's distinct pair-bearing count; z = (TR0 - interpolated mean) / interpolated SD; |z| <= 2: row count explains TR0's dimension; |z| > 2: corpus identity does; also whether TR0 lies inside the min-max envelope interpolated between the bracketing sizes. Reported alongside the range test, not instead of it.

matched_size_control.rule: per configuration, recorded BEFORE anything else is interpreted: with r = [min, max] of the 8 matched-size Rfam subsamples' nontrivial dimension, ABOVE (TR0 > max) or BELOW (TR0 < min) = at matched row count the dimension depends on corpus identity (Rfam consensus projections vs bpRNA per-molecule references), direction reported; INSIDE (min <= TR0 <= max) = it does not, so the measurement is a property of the model's structure space rather than of a corpus and Rfam's 214 stops being a single-source number. INSIDE is an informative outcome, not a failed control, and does not void the run.

descriptive_unregistered_claude.status: descriptive and unregistered (Claude, 2026-10-10); every SE combines the sampling error of each mean involved

evidence_from_this_artifact.independence: each saturation size draws with SeedSequence([seed, size]) and the matched-size control with SeedSequence([seed, 0]), each a fresh draw without replacement from the same population, so the means are independent estimates

interpolation_not_used.why_not_used: linear in log row count across [10k, 30k], while the curve's slope reverses at or near 10k (note_claude), so the straight line is not supported as an estimate of the curve at 11,955 rows; a direct measurement at exactly that row count supersedes it (reason_user)

joint_read.kind: registered test invalidated by its own data; not a result
joint_read.note_claude: Resolved: the seed-mean curve turns over at or near the bracket's lower end. It changes by +78.9 from 3k to 10k (+4.89 SE) and by -72.4 from 10k to 30k (-4.70 SE); its slope per ln(rows) changes by -131.4 at 10k (-4.96 SE). Not resolved: where the maximum lies relative to the bracket (the direct point at 11,955 rows exceeds the 10k mean by 13.4, 0.78 SE), and the direct point's departure from the line (25.1, 1.66 SE once the line's own sampling error is included). A curve non-increasing on [10k, 30k] is therefore not rejected; the premise these data leave unsupported is the one linear interpolation needs, approximate linearity in log row count across the bracket, because the slope reverses at its lower end. The supersession needs no interpolation premise: the matched-size control is a direct measurement at exactly 11,955 rows, by the same procedure, configuration and population as the saturation run.
joint_read.premise: predictions.joint_read states no validity condition; interpolating linearly in log row count presumes the seed-mean curve is approximately linear in log row count across the bracket
